u13:
The discussion generally goes straight to "should people be monogamous or free-love?" but as I discuss in my Romance Guide, this is one level too late in the conversation. The community problem is that close quarters make jealousy bigger, and jealousy can capture either system.

If people are doing rigid monogamy, it can turn their fear and possession into a moral law. If people are doing free love, but aren't doing the inner pl/ork, it can just give them a larger spreadsheet to distribute the same fear over. Calling relationships by this or that name doesn't release childhood panic, or comparison, or the terror of being abandoned, or the wish to control another person.
u14:
The non-negotiable for me is that jealousy can't become the hidden governor. This doesn't mean it can't come up. It needs to be able to be talked about, and to be felt in the body. It needs to be explored without humiliation. And it needs to be let go of gradually, not turned into punishment or policy.

There are ways the group can help, and basic boundaries the group can enforce, without deciding what type of relationships people have. Even so, there will still be disagreements about this. That's more realistic than saying it's all been resolved.
